title: 工作流 vs 智能体
author: Salmon Joy
content:
Workflow vs Agent: Deterministic Orchestration & Dynamic Tool Selection

Quick Diagnosis

Situation Recommended approach Why it fits
All steps known ahead of time (e.g., fetch data → prompt → parse → store) Workflow Immutable execution, easy testing, predictable token usage
Path depends on content or user intent (e.g., “answer any compliance question”) Agent Chooses tools at runtime, handles unknown sub‑tasks
Regulatory audit required (immutable logs, version‑controlled prompts) Workflow Deterministic runs produce repeatable audit trails
Live numeric value needed (credit score, market rate) Tool call from workflow (authoritative API) Guarantees freshness; does not rely on stale retrieval
Batch processing with tight cost budget Workflow One LLM call per step, predictable token usage
Real‑time, ad‑hoc question answering Agent Dynamic reasoning, on‑the‑fly tool selection
Mix of known skeleton + occasional live‑value request Hybrid (workflow + runtime API/agent) Keeps core deterministic, adds flexibility only where required

Decision Flow

flowchart TD
    A["Is the full execution path known ahead of time?"]
    B["Can every required tool be enumerated?"]
    C["Use a deterministic workflow"]
    D["Is the request likely to need unknown sub‑tasks?"]
    E["Add an agent layer for dynamic tool selection"]
    F["Can live values be fetched via an API?"]
    G["Expose API call from the workflow"]
    H["Leave decision to the agent at runtime"]

    A -->|Yes| B
    B -->|Yes| C
    B -->|No| D
    D -->|Yes| E
    D -->|No| F
    F -->|Yes| G
    F -->|No| H

Architectural Responsibilities

Layer Core duty Typical implementation
Deterministic Orchestrator Define the fixed sequence, validate inputs, enforce business rules, emit immutable logs Azure Logic Apps, Temporal, Airflow, hand‑rolled Python DAG
Agent Core Detect intent, decide which tool or retrieval source to invoke, manage ReAct‑style loops, handle fall‑backs LLM prompting with function‑calling schema, structured reasoning templates
Tool / Retrieval Layer Provide static knowledge (document store) or fresh data (authoritative API) Azure Cognitive Search, public REST endpoints, token‑protected credit‑bureau API
Governance & Auditing Record every step, version‑control prompts, certify compliance checks Write‑once log storage, signed manifests, CI linting of workflow definitions
Cost & Latency Monitor Track token usage, external‑API count, per‑step latency OpenTelemetry exporters, custom metric dashboards

Python Decision Helper (Teaching‑Only)

# decision_helper.py – pure stdlib, no external packages
import json
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Literal, TypedDict

class DecisionInput(TypedDict):
    """Minimal data required to pick workflow vs. agent."""
    steps_known: bool          # True if the entire sequence can be enumerated
    tools_enumerated: bool     # True if every tool can be listed up‑front
    live_value_needed: bool    # True if an authoritative API must be called
    dynamic_subtasks: bool     # True if request may spawn unknown sub‑tasks

def choose_strategy(data: DecisionInput) -> Literal["workflow", "agent", "hybrid"]:
    """
    Return the recommended execution style.

    * `workflow` – fully deterministic pipeline
    * `agent`    – pure agentic control
    * `hybrid`   – deterministic skeleton with optional runtime API or agent
    """
    # Basic validation – fail fast if the contract is broken
    assert isinstance(data["steps_known"], bool), "steps_known must be bool"
    assert isinstance(data["tools_enumerated"], bool), "tools_enumerated must be bool"
    assert isinstance(data["live_value_needed"], bool), "live_value_needed must be bool"
    assert isinstance(data["dynamic_subtasks"], bool), "dynamic_subtasks must be bool"

    if data["steps_known"] and data["tools_enumerated"]:
        # All actions are known → deterministic flow
        return "workflow"
    if data["dynamic_subtasks"]:
        # Content can generate new branches → need agentic reasoning
        return "agent"
    # Mixed case – known skeleton but may need live data or optional tool selection
    return "hybrid"

# -------------------------------------------------
# Example usage (for teaching only – not part of production)
if __name__ == "__main__":
    example = {
        "steps_known": True,
        "tools_enumerated": True,
        "live_value_needed": False,
        "dynamic_subtasks": False,
    }
    print(json.dumps({"strategy": choose_strategy(example)}))

Teaching‑Only Note – Production systems should encode this decision in a CI‑validated configuration file rather than an ad‑hoc script.

Architectural Decision Records (ADRs)

ADR 1 – Introducing an Agent for Policy Queries

Context

A fintech onboarding pipeline executes three fixed steps (identity → credit → welcome email). Occasionally, a regulator submits a policy_query that does not fit the fixed path.

Decision

Add an optional agent that is triggered only when the incoming payload contains a policy_query field. The agent will invoke a policy‑search tool, retrieve the relevant text, and attach it to the final output.

Consequences

  • The core majority of requests remain in a deterministic workflow, preserving auditability.
  • New logs capture the agent’s chosen tool, LLM prompt, and tool response, enabling traceability.
  • Latency impact is limited to the subset of requests that require the agent.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. Agent‑enabled paths generate a log entry that records the selected tool, the exact prompt sent to the LLM, and the tool’s raw response.
  2. All agent‑generated outputs are stored with a cryptographic hash for integrity verification.
  3. CI pipeline includes unit tests for both “with query” and “without query” scenarios, and validates that the workflow remains deterministic when the agent is not invoked.

ADR 2 – Handling Live Credit‑Limit Values

Context

The onboarding flow must embed the applicant’s current credit limit, which changes frequently. A stale document store could return an outdated figure.

Decision

Expose a tool in the workflow that calls the credit‑bureau’s authoritative REST endpoint. The workflow pauses, fetches the live limit, and continues deterministically. No caching of the numeric value is permitted.

Consequences

  • Guarantees freshness of a critical compliance datum.
  • Introduces a single external API call per onboarding, which is observable in cost‑monitoring dashboards.
  • Enables deterministic testing by mocking the API response within a test harness.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. Integration tests with a mock endpoint produce the same structural response shape as the real service.
  2. Production logs record request‑ID, endpoint URL, response timestamp, and the returned numeric value.
  3. Any failure to reach the API aborts the workflow with a defined error code and escalates to a human reviewer.

Evaluation & Maintenance Checklist

  • Functional correctness

    • ✅ Deterministic steps produce identical output for identical inputs (regression suite).
    • ✅ Agent‑enabled paths have mocked‑LLM tests covering tool selection logic.

  • Governance

    • ✅ Prompt templates are version‑controlled, signed, and reviewed.
    • ✅ Business rules (e.g., “identity verification before credit check”) live in code, not in LLM prompts.

  • Cost visibility

    • ✅ Token usage per step logged to a cost‑center dashboard.
    • ✅ External‑API call count tracked; alerts trigger on abnormal spikes.

  • Latency observability

    • ✅ End‑to‑end latency recorded; thresholds defined per SLA.
    • ✅ Separate latency metric for agent loops to bound their impact.

  • Knowledge freshness

    • ✅ Retrieval index (Azure Cognitive Search) refreshed on a schedule aligned with policy updates.
    • ✅ Live‑value endpoints re‑validated after any vendor version change.

  • Model updates

    • ✅ Prompting is the first line of defence; LoRA fine‑tuning is applied only after a documented gap analysis shows prompting insufficient.
    • ✅ When LoRA is applied, a full regression suite on pre‑existing deterministic tests is run; behavior preservation is not assumed.

  • Security & Auditing

    • ✅ Secrets stored in a vault; never hard‑coded.
    • ✅ Execution logs are immutable, encrypted, and retained per compliance window.

References

  • Microsoft Retrieval‑Augmented Generation concepts – https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/retrieval-augmented-generation
  • “LoRA: Low‑Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models” – https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.09685

summary: 本文探讨了确定性工作流与自主 AI 智能体之间的结构性权衡。文章基于执行路径可预测性、审计要求以及对实时数据的需求，提供了一套决策矩阵。作者梳理了分层职责，并为金融科技入驻等真实场景提供了架构决策记录（ADR），强调治理与成本效率。

mainPoints.explanation: 当所有步骤都提前已知时，应使用工作流，以确保不可变性、易于测试以及可预测的 token 用量。
当执行路径取决于用户意图，或需要通过动态工具选择来处理未知子任务时，智能体是必要的。
混合模式保留确定性的骨架，仅在需要灵活性或实时价值请求的地方叠加智能体层。
系统应将确定性编排器、智能体核心、工具/检索层与治理监控分离。

keyQuotes: 确定性运行会产生可重复的审计轨迹
任务不是读取标签，而是知道标签没有说什么
确定性，仅在需要之处增加灵活性
